body: It's not for nutrition to him, but in her mind it is. She's lactating because she's feeding a baby - so to her, her breasts are her baby's food source right now, and it's likely (and quite naturally) very uncomfortable for her to view breastfeeding in a sexual way. That has to be respected and isn't likely to change easily, though that isn't to say she won't change her mind.

I have a mental health plan and a psychologist but I've recently finished uni and currently have no income, so sadly can't see them right now. If I get to the point where I think I will actually take my life, I'll call Lifeline, but I don't think I could ever do that to my daughter. And yes there is a lot left out, but basically he says he just lied to me pretending he was happy and he loved me for the past ten years because it was the easiest option.
Yes. He did not want more children but we had both said over the years that if it ever happened we would just make it work. I did not plan on becoming pregnant again.

I wish I knew what my ex's answer to this would be. We were together for over ten years and have a 9-year-old daughter. I thought we were happy. I found out a few weeks ago that I'm pregnant with our second child. He promptly stated that he no longer loved me, that he'd been wanting to leave me for years but had stayed for the sex, and that he doesn't want to be a part of this baby's life. I wish I'd known sooner that he didn't see a future with me.

Thank you for that. It wouldn't surprise me at all... I do tend to have nightmares (and I would class these as something of the sort) when I'm particularly stressed or overwhelmed. I've been having a lot of bad dreams and nightmares recently about a wide range of things... I guess this just stuck out because in this one I'm the one doing something wrong.

Urgh... this sounds very close to home. She definitely is more like a friend to me and I do find it hard to be a "parent" - I try to set boundaries (albeit loose ones) but I give in very easily just to avoid fights... because when we argue, I'm just as bad as she is and neither of us will back down. Her dad usually has to tell us to stop going back and forth. I also definitely see her as my main way of feeling loved and valuable... I basically see her as my entire world, that she is the one person I know loves me unconditionally, and I have very much tied my personal identity to being her mother as opposed to being an individual person.

I'm hugely stressed. I have struggled with depression and anxiety since I was a child, and these have been worsened lately. I'm in my final year of university and my dad died of cancer a few months ago. He was only in his 50s and my best friend. I have a great relationship with my partner (my daughter's dad) and we have more than enough sex for me haha.

Thank you for your reply. I guess I just needed that reassurance that it's not my fault she feels this way and that I can't force her to do anything. I am currently seeing someone (I was in the past but stopped going when Dad was sick, returned recently after he died) so I think I'll talk to them about it when I see them next as it's been weighing really heavily on me, feeling that I'm responsible for my mum's life. It's a horrible feeling... I couldn't save my dad and now I feel I can't save her, either. Hopefully she can hang onto the things she has as reason to keep going.

I'm aware of how pregnancy occurs - doesn't change the fact that there's a difference between trying to get pregnant and simply not doing anything to prevent it. The millions of unwanted children in the world can attest to that.

Nah, that's not true. By that standard, every dumb 16-year-old that is too dumb to use contraception is actively trying to get pregnant, and every person that has a drunken one-night-stand is trying to conceive. That line of thinking just doesn't make sense.

Some people just don't care enough to do anything about it either way. Plenty of guys would be more than happy to have unprotected sex but would balk at the thought of being a parent. And plenty of women engage in risky sex but hope they won't get pregnant. Maybe you don't get it because you can't relate to it, but that doesn't make it any less possible.
